fullPassage: In 2025, a team of researchers at the MIT Media Lab conducted an experiment that swiftly captured international attention. Volunteers were divided into three groups and instructed to write essays under different conditions: one group used ChatGPT, another relied on a conventional search engine, and the third wrote entirely unaided. While the participants composed their essays, the researchers monitored their brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG). The results were striking: the group that used ChatGPT exhibited markedly weaker neural connectivity than the other two, and their essays were judged by human evaluators to be less original. More surprisingly still, when these same participants were later asked to write without any AI assistance, their brain activity remained noticeably subdued compared to that of participants who had never used AI in the first place. The researchers termed this phenomenon "cognitive debt"—a short-term gain in efficiency that may come at the expense of long-term independent thinking. Although the study remains preliminary, it has already prompted many educators to reconsider how AI ought to be integrated into the classroom.

det.tip: markedly ≈ significantly — 둘 다 '현저히, 눈에 띄게'. markedly weaker = 현저히 더 약한

questions.passage: In 2025, a team of researchers at the MIT Media Lab conducted an experiment that swiftly captured international attention. Volunteers were divided into three groups and instructed to write essays under different conditions: one group used ChatGPT, another relied on a conventional search engine, and the third wrote entirely unaided. While the participants composed their essays, the researchers monitored their brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG). The results were striking: the group that used ChatGPT exhibited markedly <u>weaker</u> neural connectivity than the other two, and their essays were judged by human evaluators to be less original. More surprisingly still, when these same participants were later asked to write without any AI assistance, their brain activity remained noticeably subdued compared to that of participants who had never used AI in the first place. The researchers termed this phenomenon "cognitive debt"—a short-term gain in efficiency that may come at the expense of long-term independent thinking. Although the study remains preliminary, it has already prompted many educators to reconsider how AI ought to be integrated into the classroom.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 weaker와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① lighter — 더 가벼운. 무게를 나타내 weaker의 직접 반의어가 아님
✅ ② stronger — 더 강한. weaker(더 약한)의 직접적 반의어로 뜻이 가장 멂
❌ ③ smaller — 더 작은. 크기를 나타내 의미축이 달라 반의어가 아님
❌ ④ softer — 더 부드러운. 강도의 반대는 되지만 세기(strength)의 직접 반의어는 stronger임
det.tip: weaker(더 약한) ↔ stronger(더 강한). markedly weaker neural connectivity = 현저히 더 약한 신경 연결성

More surprisingly still, when these same participants were later asked to write without any AI assistance, their brain activity remained noticeably subdued compared to that of participants who had never used AI in the first place. The researchers termed this phenomenon "cognitive debt"—a short-term gain in efficiency that may come at the expense of long-term independent thinking. Although the study remains <u>preliminary</u>, it has already prompted many educators to reconsider how AI ought to be integrated into the classroom.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 preliminary와 의미가 가장 먼 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① initial — 초기의. preliminary(예비적인)와 비슷한 방향이라 '가장 먼' 것이 아님
❌ ② tentative — 잠정적인. preliminary와 유사한 뜻이라 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ experimental — 실험적인. 아직 확정되지 않았다는 점에서 preliminary와 결이 비슷함
✅ ④ conclusive — 결정적인, 확정적인. preliminary(예비적인)의 직접적 반의어로 뜻이 가장 멂
det.tip: preliminary(예비적) ↔ conclusive(결정적). initial/tentative는 오히려 비슷한 뜻이라 함정

questions.passage:
(A) In the MIT study, the volunteers were asked to write essays under three different <u>conditions</u>, and each group was given a different tool.

(B) After years of overwork and stress, the journalist developed a serious heart <u>condition</u> that eventually forced her to stop working.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)의 밑줄 친 condition(s)의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 조건, 상황 — (B) 질환, 질병: (A) under three different conditions = 세 가지 다른 조건에서(조건/상황) / (B) a serious heart condition = 심각한 심장 질환(질병)
❌ ② (A) 질환, 질병 — (B) 조건, 상황: (A)(B)의 의미가 뒤바뀌어 부적절
❌ ③ (A) 상태 — (B) 조건, 상황: (A)는 실험의 '조건'을 뜻하지 단순 '상태'가 아니며 (B)도 '질환'이라 어긋남
❌ ④ (A) 조건, 상황 — (B) 상태: (B) heart condition은 '심장 질환'이라는 병명이지 일반적 '상태'가 아님
det.tip: condition의 다의: ① 조건/상황(under different conditions) ② 질환/질병(a heart condition)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one that is unusual or difficult to fully explain"

det.korean: 관찰되는, 특히 설명하기 어려운 사실이나 현상 → phenomenon(현상)
det.analysis:
❌ ① hypothesis — 가설. 검증되지 않은 '추정'이지 관찰되는 사실/현상 자체가 아님
❌ ② procedure — 절차. 일을 진행하는 방법이나 순서를 뜻해 정의와 다름
✅ ③ phenomenon — 현상. '관찰되는, 특히 특이하거나 설명하기 어려운 사실이나 상황'이라는 정의에 정확히 부합
❌ ④ coincidence — 우연의 일치. 우연히 동시에 일어난 일을 뜻해 정의와 다름
det.tip: phenomenon = 현상. termed this phenomenon 'cognitive debt' = 이 현상을 '인지 부채'라 명명함

questions.passage: While the participants composed their essays, the researchers monitored their brain activity __________ (use) electroencephalography (EEG).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: '~을 사용하여'라는 부대상황을 나타내는 분사구문이므로 현재분사 → using
det.analysis: 정답: using — 주절(the researchers monitored their brain activity) 뒤에서 '~을 사용하면서/사용하여'라는 동시 동작·수단을 나타내는 분사구문이 필요하므로 현재분사 using으로 바꿔 쓴다. use → using. monitored ... using EEG = 뇌전도를 사용하여 관찰했다
det.tip: 동사가 부대상황(~하면서/하여)을 나타내면 현재분사(-ing). using EEG = EEG를 사용하여

questions.passage: The results were striking: the group that used ChatGPT exhibited markedly __________ (weak) neural connectivity than the other two, and their essays were judged by human evaluators to be less original.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 뒤에 비교 대상 than이 있으므로 비교급 → weaker
det.analysis: 정답: weaker — 뒤에 'than the other two(다른 두 집단보다)'라는 비교 대상이 이어지므로 형용사 weak의 비교급이 필요하다. 1음절 형용사는 -er을 붙여 비교급을 만든다. weak → weaker. markedly weaker ... than = 현저히 더 약한
det.tip: than이 보이면 비교급. 1음절 형용사는 -er. weak → weaker(더 약한)

questions.passage: In 2025, a team of researchers at the MIT Media Lab conducted an experiment that swiftly captured international attention. Volunteers were divided into three groups and instructed to write essays under different conditions: one group used ChatGPT, another relied on a conventional search engine, and the third wrote entirely unaided. More surprisingly still, when these same participants were later asked to write without any AI assistance, their brain activity remained noticeably subdued compared to that of participants who had never used AI in the first place. The researchers termed this phenomenon "__________"—a short-term gain in efficiency that may come at the expense of long-term independent thinking. Although the study remains preliminary, it has already prompted many educators to reconsider how AI ought to be integrated into the classroom.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 단기적 효율성을 얻는 대신 장기적 사고를 잃는 현상을 부르는 이름 → cognitive debt(인지 부채)
det.analysis:
❌ ① mental profit — 정신적 이익. 뒤에 이어지는 '장기적 사고를 희생시키는 대가'라는 부정적 설명과 어울리지 않음
✅ ② cognitive debt — 인지 부채. 대시(—) 뒤의 '단기적 효율성의 이득이 장기적 독립적 사고를 희생시킬 수 있다'는 설명이 '부채(빚)'라는 비유에 정확히 부합
❌ ③ digital fluency — 디지털 능숙도. 능력의 향상을 뜻해 대가·희생이라는 설명과 맞지 않음
❌ ④ creative liberty — 창작의 자유. 자유를 뜻해 뒤의 부정적 설명과 어울리지 않음
det.tip: termed this phenomenon 'cognitive debt' — 대시 뒤 설명(단기 이득 vs 장기 대가)이 '부채(debt)' 비유의 단서

questions.passage: In 2025, a team of researchers at the MIT Media Lab conducted an experiment that swiftly captured international attention. Volunteers were divided into three groups and instructed to write essays under different conditions: one group used ChatGPT, another relied on a conventional search engine, and the third wrote entirely unaided. While the participants composed their essays, the researchers monitored their brain activity using electroencephalography (EEG). The results were striking: the group that used ChatGPT exhibited markedly weaker neural connectivity than the other two, and their essays were judged by human evaluators to be less original. More surprisingly still, when these same participants were later asked to write without any AI assistance, their brain activity remained noticeably subdued compared to that of participants who had never used AI in the first place. The researchers termed this phenomenon "cognitive debt"—a short-term gain in efficiency that may come at the expense of long-term independent thinking. Although the study remains preliminary, it has already prompted many educators to reconsider how AI ought to be __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 교육자들이 AI가 어떻게 '교실에 통합되어야' 하는지 재고하게 됨 → integrated into the classroom
det.analysis:
❌ ① removed from all schools — 모든 학교에서 제거되다. '어떻게 ~되어야 하는지 재고한다'는 흐름은 완전 제거가 아니라 도입 방식의 재검토임
❌ ② banned during examinations — 시험 중 금지되다. 시험이라는 구체적 상황은 본문에 언급되지 않음
❌ ③ taught as a subject — 하나의 과목으로 가르쳐지다. AI를 교과목으로 가르치는 문제는 다루지 않음
✅ ④ integrated into the classroom — 교실에 통합되다. 인지 부채 우려로 교육자들이 'AI가 어떻게 교실에 통합되어야 하는지' 재고하게 되었다는 흐름에 정확히 부합
det.tip: reconsider how AI ought to be integrated into the classroom = AI를 교실에 어떻게 통합할지 재고하다
